title: Logic gates from a single NAND
task: Using only `nand(a, b)` (given) and your own gates, write `not_(a)`, `and_(a, b)`, `or_(a, b)` and `xor_(a, b)`. Each takes bits (0 or 1) and returns a bit. No Python operators, `if`, or comparisons: just calls.
hints: Work from the tables. Compare the AND column with the NAND table: what's the relationship? For OR, re-read the De Morgan sentence. For XOR, re-read "at least one is on, and not both".
`and_` is NOT of a NAND. `or_` is a NAND of the two inverted inputs. `xor_` is an AND of two things you already have: "at least one" (OR) and "not both" (NAND).
`and_`: `not_(nand(a, b))`. `or_`: `nand(not_(a), not_(b))`. `xor_`: `and_(or_(a, b), nand(a, b))`. (The 4-NAND version: `n = nand(a, b)`, then `nand(nand(a, n), nand(b, n))`.)

quiz.why: NAND is 0 only when both inputs are 1. Here one is 0, so it's 1.

options.why: Try a = 1, b = 0: the inputs become 0 and 1, and NAND of those is 1. AND would give 0.
Try a = 1, b = 1: the inputs become 0 and 0, and NAND gives 1. XOR would give 0.
It's De Morgan: not (not a and not b) is a or b. It's 0 only when both a and b are 0.
NOR is 1 only when both inputs are 0. This is 0 exactly then, so it's the opposite of NOR.

review.why: XOR is 1 only when the inputs differ. 1 and 1 are the same, so it's 0.

review.q: Which gate is `not_(nand(a, b))`? Name it.
review.why: NAND is NOT AND, so NOT of NAND is AND again.
